clue.text: Boatman's craft — they follow a pattern

definitions.meaning: small fast sailing vessels, the kind of craft a boatman handles
tailoring workers who shape cloth along the lines of a paper template

explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym is Boatman, so 'Boatman's craft' is both a self-reference and a plain description of boats.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: single-masted boats, and the garment workers who slice fabric to a template.

clue.text: Notably Picasso: Pablo's heart is in fashion

indicators.note: in puts the letters inside the word for fashion

parts.note: to cut is to shape or fashion something

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Picasso's heart is in fashion, an art-world remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Picasso co-founded the movement that broke subjects into geometric shapes, so he is the prime example of one.

clue.text: Postings on internet article about Republican promotion

definitions.note: plural description of a single noun: one chain of online posts

indicators.note: the article goes about, i.e. around, the abbreviation

parts.note: the is the definite article
an ad is an advertisement, a promotion

explanation.surface: An online article about a Republican's promotion draws postings.
explanation.definitionFit: On a forum, a chain of replies on one topic is called by this name.

clue.text: Dealer's left distributing the LSD and ecstasy

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: distributing spreads the letters out into a new order

explanation.surface: A drug dealer has left, distributing LSD and ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dealer' is a card dealer, not a drug dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games the player seated to the dealer's left, who leads first, is given this title.

clue.text: Always after second part

indicators.note: after places the word for always after the abbreviation

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: A second part always comes after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To part things is to cut or separate them, a synonym for slicing apart.

clue.text: Belt and cuff

definitions.meaning: to belt someone is to hit them hard
to cuff someone is to strike them with an open hand

explanation.walkthrough: Belt and cuff look like items of clothing, and CLOBBER is also British slang for clothes, so the surface itself hints at the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for striking someone, and clobbering is a heavy blow or beating.

clue.text: Scorpion's tail in sorry mess, caught in mug of sweet goo

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are caught inside the drinking vessel

parts.note: a mug is a cup

indicators.note: in puts the scorpion's tail inside the jumbled letters
a mess suggests the letters are jumbled
the tail of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A scorpion's tail ends up in a sorry mess, caught in a mug of sticky syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' signals the jumble and 'tail' the last letter; 'in' and 'caught in' are the two insertions. 'mug' is a drinking vessel here, not a face or a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a thick sweet syrup made from maize starch, used in American baking.

clue.text: Exclusively fashioned from nylon, but unfinished

indicators.note: fashioned means made into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
unfinished means the last letter is cut off

explanation.surface: Something made exclusively from nylon, but left unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the last letter of NYLON to leave NYLO, and 'fashioned' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean solely, with nothing else included.

clue.text: Central Birmingham, in short a city initially chap finds a pain

parts.note: B1 is the postcode for central Birmingham, read as B and ONE

indicators.note: initially means the first letter is taken

parts.note: a chap is a he, a male

explanation.surface: A man in central Birmingham finds the city a pain.
explanation.walkthrough: UK postcodes begin with a city's letters: central Birmingham is B1, so the B and the figure one spelt out supply the opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic term for an aching in the skeleton, which is a kind of physical pain.

clue.text: Energy absorbed by tenants goes back in

indicators.note: absorbed by means taken inside the other word

parts.note: renters are tenants, people who rent
E is the abbreviation for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Energy is soaked up by tenants going back into their homes.
explanation.definitionFit: To return into a place is to come in once more.

clue.text: Upset with neglect of the sick

indicators.note: neglecting something means leaving it out, so the word 'the' is dropped from the synonym

parts.note: upset means bothered, troubled

explanation.surface: Someone is upset that sick people are being neglected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the sick' reads as a group of patients, but 'the' is the letters removed and 'sick' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sick of something means being weary and fed up with it, which is a synonym for that state.

clue.text: Acrimony from Van Gogh, familiarly taking on authority

indicators.note: the painter's short name takes on board, i.e. holds within it, the word for authority

parts.note: Vincent van Gogh, shortened in a familiar way to Vince
rule means authority, dominion

explanation.surface: A bitter outburst from the painter as he takes on the establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe bitter, venomous hostility in speech or feeling.

clue.text: Sewer rat messes about on top of sludge

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around and rearranged
the top of a word in an across clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A rat in the sewers scrabbles around on a layer of sludge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' reads as a drain to suit the rat and sludge, but it is one who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who sews for a living is a sewer in the needlework sense, pronounced to rhyme with 'grower'.

clue.text: Tuck and run

definitions.meaning: in dressmaking a tuck is a stitched fold that shapes a garment
to run is to move quickly, to dash

explanation.definitionFit: In sewing it is a tapered stitched fold, and as a verb it means to move suddenly and fast.

clue.text: Battle over tirade that is the first to shatter bonds

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the next

parts.note: war means battle, conflict
a rant is a tirade
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A battle over a tirade is the first thing to shatter the bonds between people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bonds' looks like ties of friendship, but means guarantees.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond is a binding promise or guarantee, and guarantees on goods are the plural.

clue.text: He hears bard spinning yarn supplied by him

definitions.note: a description of a person: the one who supplies yarn

indicators.note: spinning suggests the letters are whirled about into a new order, punning on spinning yarn

explanation.surface: A man listens to a poet telling a long story, spinning a yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning yarn' looks like storytelling; 'spinning' is the anagram signal and 'yarn' is wool or thread.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer in sewing goods sells thread, ribbons, buttons and wool, so wool comes from his shop.

clue.text: Told to carry actual train in vessel for last journey

indicators.note: told means spoken, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: carry is bear, actual is real, train in is learn: bear-real-learn said quickly

explanation.surface: Someone is told to carry a real train in a vessel, an odd instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carry actual train in' becomes BEAR REAL LEARN, which said aloud approximates the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot for cremated ashes accompanies the dead on their final passage, the funeral.

clue.text: What 19s can achieve, if put back in wardrobe

indicators.note: in places the reversed word inside the cupboard

parts.note: a closet is a wardrobe, a cupboard for clothes

indicators.note: put back means turned round, so the word is reversed

explanation.surface: What tailors can achieve if their work is put back in the wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: '19s' are the answer to 19 down, tailors; 'put back' turns IF into FI.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailors cut garments to hug the body exactly, a snug result that ready-made clothes rarely achieve.

clue.text: Suggest getting close

definitions.meaning: to suggest is to hint or imply indirectly
close in a personal sense: familiar, near, as in a close friendship

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to hint, and the adjective means very familiar, near in friendship.

clue.text: He sold material, part of scripts, writing in and changing each

definitions.note: describes a person: a man who sold cloth

parts.note: a line is one part of a script spoken by an actor

indicators.note: in puts the writing letter inside the rearranged word
changing means the letters of 'and' are put in a different order

parts.note: R stands for writing, one of the three Rs (reading, writing and arithmetic)
per means each, as in 'a pound per head'

explanation.surface: A writer of scripts revises them, writing things in and changing each part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges AND into NDA, and 'in' puts R inside it to give NDRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A draper is a cloth merchant, and this kind specialised in fabric woven from flax.

clue.text: Boatman changes heading: he knows how to tack

indicators.note: changes heading means the first letter is replaced by another

parts.note: a sailor is a boatman

explanation.surface: A boatman changes course: he knows how to tack into the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes heading' and 'tack' both sound like sailing; tack here means sew loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: To tack is to sew with long temporary stitches, a basic skill of a clothes maker.

clue.text: Boatman to join a navy

parts.note: a seam is where two pieces of cloth are joined

explanation.surface: A boatman goes to join a navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor, especially one below officer rank, works aboard boats and ships.

clue.text: 19 reflecting the tools of his trade

definitions.note: the solution to 19 down, a maker of clothes

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the other way round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: pins are the tools a tailor works with

explanation.surface: A clothes maker considers the tools of his trade.
explanation.walkthrough: '19' refers to the answer to 19 down, TAILOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Snip is old British slang for a maker of suits, from the sound of his shears.

clue.text: Reserve falling away finally, natural to be in stitches

indicators.note: the final letter of the word falls away, i.e. is removed

parts.note: a cache is a hidden reserve or store
innate means natural, inborn

explanation.surface: Losing one's reserve and laughing naturally until in stitches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in stitches' hints at sewing, matching the theme, but here means laughing helplessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in stitches means laughing uncontrollably, and the rare verb means to laugh loudly.

clue.text: Addiction to gear

definitions.meaning: a compulsion one cannot break, as in a drug dependency
clothing or outfit, as in a monk's or a riding outfit

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a compulsive practice, and also a distinctive garment such as a nun's robe.

clue.text: Other people set Tory leader on edge

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first piece on top of the next
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a hem is the edge of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: Other people put the Tory leader on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun refers to a group of people other than the speaker or listener.

clue.text: Little time to cry about source of light for picture

parts.note: a flash is a very brief moment, as in 'in a flash'

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to blub is to cry, weep

explanation.surface: Someone has little time to cry over a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Old cameras used a single-use bulb giving a burst of light to illuminate the photograph.

clue.text: Faith, by itself, aims for only half its members to be seen

indicators.text: for only half its members to be seen
indicators.note: showing only half the letters means taking every other one, starting from the first

explanation.surface: A faith, on its own, aims to have only half its congregation seen in public.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters of 'itself aims' are I, S, L, A and M.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the religion of Muslims, one of the major world faiths.

clue.text: Orchestra's leader getting in tune at start of new film

indicators.note: the letter gets into the word for tune, sitting inside it

parts.note: a theme is a melody, a tune

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
the start of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An orchestra's leader gets in tune at the start of a new film score.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a 1976 horror movie about the Antichrist child Damien.

clue.text: You might score one after international trial

indicators.note: after puts the scoring word after the international

parts.note: a Test is an international match, especially in cricket
in cricket a run is what a batsman scores

explanation.surface: A batsman might score a run after an international trial match.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international cricket fixture, and runs are cricket's scoring unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal or practice go to see whether something works is a trial.
